failure_summary: Both runs fail A6 (pre-computed: prose never names column 4) even though the assembled prompt states "Better move: column 4 (lands at c4r4)" verbatim and offers [zone:col4] with role "the column of the better move", and both fail G2 by ignoring link.guardrail ("name both lines with their horizons") — neither the forced win completing at c2r5 (28 plies, real on the engine finalMovestring 33322232332414001244445556666660011) nor the opponent win at c2r4 is named; production-fidelity caveat: model is gpt-5.4-mini, the shipped model, so prompt_confusion here cannot be separated from model capability.
notes: Only 2 runs in this run-set (run_index 0..1), so the v1 sub-sampling rule (A3/A4/G2/G4/G5 on first 2 runs) covers every run — no nulls recorded. A1/A2/A6 and G7a/G7b_offered copied verbatim from fv_suff_answers_boards_2026-08-06T16-04-29Z_served_mechanical.json (A6=fail both runs, G7a/G7b=pass both). A6: run0 says "the central column that keeps more four-in-a-row lines alive", run1 "the more central column" — neither names column 4; this is exactly the trigger production mentionsBetterColumn uses, so production would have retried these. G2 (both runs): guardrail unhonored — run0 names only "a winning line for them" with no cell/line/horizon and never says you gave up a WIN (it says you gave up "the 7-shaped double threat idea"); run1 never mentions the opponent forcing a win at all and downgrades the forced win to "kept your winning chances open longer". Anchoring for those lines was never offered at this vintage: render_decision.zones.aliases = [better-col(col4), played-col(col7)] only and requiredSet=[] , so the deep-line half of the guardrail is a render-layer gap (missing_info), not a model failure — I graded against the recorded render_decision per Step 0, NOT against the Step 0b prompt I rebuilt with current code, which anachronistically offers and REQUIRES you-future-fork / you-key-line / opp-key-square that the 08-06 run never saw. A7b (run 0 only): "the 7-shaped double threat idea in the center" is a specific-sounding board object wrapped only in [term:figure_7] — a glossary popup that highlights nothing — with no cell named and no zone available to anchor it; figure_7 itself is real (lostResource.tacticTag=figure_7, tacticCells c5r3/c4r4/c5r5/c4r5/c3r5, fork at c2r5 on the projectedDeep board), so this is missing_info (no zone offered for it), not fabrication. A7c not charged: no *-fork-pivot handle exists in render_decision.zones.aliases. G1 (both runs): "the tougher book continuation" asserts opening-book provenance that render_decision.openingContext.lead denies outright (id/family/matchedPrefixLen/bookCol/holdCol all null; frameId O3 centrality) and that the opening reading key explicitly forbids ("This position matches no named opening or defense line"); it is also misleading, telling the player column 4 is right because it is book rather than because it holds a forced win. "Tougher/resilient" wording is render-supplied (replyHistogram reading key) and is NOT charged. A3/A4 pass both runs: verified on ./visualize_board.sh 333222 (solver row: col4=+3 win, col7=-2 loss, confirming win_to_lose) — the only concrete claims are the two columns and the center-located figure_7, all board-true. A5 pass both: 2nd person, no player names, no field names; A5b N/A (player===1). G3 pass (afterBest/afterPlayed omitted as tag-set-identical and neither answer needed them). G4 vacuous-pass (no cell or line named in prose). G5 pass: every projectedDeep threat-list entry is board-true — Y holds c3r5/c4r5/c5r5 so c2r5 (gravity-top over a height-4 column = immediate) and c6r5 both complete, O holds c3r6/c4r6/c5r6 so c2r6/c6r6 complete, and the Y major at c2r6 is the c2r6-c3r5-c4r4-c5r3 diagonal. G6 pass: patternOnAfterBestBoard null with link L6 is the right route for win_to_lose carrying both a lost winning_line and an opponent winning_line. G7 pass both: annotationRepairs empty, guardDiagnostics clean, and every emitted handle wraps a role-matching phrase (col4 = better column, col7 = played column, figure_7 wraps its canonical phrase); mild over-wrap on run0 col4 ("the central column that keeps more four-in-a-row lines alive") is not semantic mismatch. Intermittent=true only because A7 fails run 0 and passes run 1; A6, G1 and G2 fail deterministically on both runs. servedExplanation is byte-identical to mechanism in both rows (guard stripped nothing), so the v2 post-guard target changes no verdict here.
